title: Understanding FastAPI Versions and Compatibility
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding fastapi versions and compatibility in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to checking installed package versions.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers understanding fastapi versions and compatibility within introduction to fastapi. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use understanding fastapi versions and compatibility to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Understanding FastAPI Versions and Compatibility matters because it is part of introduction to fastapi. In practice, focus on predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Understanding FastAPI Versions and Compatibility”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Checking installed package versions” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Understanding FastAPI Versions and Compatibility, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
